text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rates for v6 traffic in us-east-az15. Alert: multiple customer 502/504s and TCP resets observed across edge gateways. Investigating. thread:1852009876

erin_oncall: I'm on it. Seeing symtom of PMTUD failures from initial traces — ICMPv6 "Packet too big" reported, but probes suppressed in some paths. Can netops confirm whether AZ15 had any network stack changes overnight?

netops_sam: No config pushes to AZ15 since 03:00Z. Network telemetry shows borderline MTU negotiation failures on a subset of edge routers that see jumbo frames (9000) from internal hosts. Looks like certain transit peers are dropping ICMPv6 PTB, causing endpoints to keep sending large packets.

ryan_sre: Confirmed customer-facing LB logs show repeated RSTs and HTTP/2 stream errors on dual-stack flows. v4-only traffic mostly fine. Impacting customers: enterprise-corp (partial), edge-pipeline (ingest).

bob_infra: Can we force-fallback those LBs to prefer IPv4 for affected backends as interim mitigation? There's a config flag to disable v6 preference per-target-group.

katie_prod: Customer Ops—start drafting a status update. Mark as partial degradation for IPv6 in us-east-az15. Link to status page once we have a clear mitigation.

customer_ops: Notifying account teams for enterprise-corp and edge-pipeline. They reported timeouts at ~11:42Z.

erin_oncall: Triage checklist: 1) Confirm ICMPv6 PTB suppression from the path (tcpdump), 2) Apply MTU clamp at ingress + edge for affected routers + set LB v6 preference off, 3) Route affected customers to cross-AZ failover if clamp insufficient. I'll run tcpdump on the egress pair now.

bob_infra: Dropping a quick tcpdump snippet from gw-az15-e3:

```
22:18:01.123456 IP6 2001:db8:aa::1 > 2600:feed::5: icmp6, packet too big, mtu 1280, length 1460
22:18:01.123789 IP 10.0.0.5 > 10.0.1.12: IP packet exceeds MTU: frag needed
```

erin_oncall: That's the PTB right there — path MTU 1280 communicated but endpoints keep sending 1500/9000. Looks like some transit dropped the PTB earlier in the path, but eventually gw reported it. Some peers are not forwarding PTB back to senders, so PMTUD stalls.

netops_sam: Quick mitigation options: A) Enforce MTU clamp to 1420 on edge router for v6 (prevents fragmentation), B) Disable IPv6 preference on LB for affected target groups (force v4), C) Announce temporary route to alternate AZ (cross-region if required). I'd recommend A+B immediately.

erin_oncall: Agreed. Applying MTU clamp to edge pair now (gwy-config cli). Will also flip LB v6_prefer=false for target group tg-enterprise-corp-us-east-az15.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: mtu-clamp/az15 -> edge-router-pair (run_id: d-98321). Rolling 2/2.

netops_sam: MTU clamp applied to edge-router-pair: set interface mtu 1420; tcpdump shows subsequent packets sized <=1420.

erin_oncall: Flipped LB v6 preference for the two affected target groups. Monitoring error rate.

ryan_sre: Early signals: 60% reduction in 502s for enterprise-corp within 2m. edge-pipeline still has intermittent timeouts (some long flows). Might need cross-AZ failover for high-throughput UDP-ish flows.

katie_prod: Posting status update: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/US-EAST-AZ15-ipv6-pmtud (draft). Marking "partial IPv6 connectivity degraded for some customers in us-east-az15".

customer_ops: Customers notified. A couple of self-serve users saw immediate recovery after v6->v4 fallback. Enterprise-corp getting workaround instructions to pin IPv4 or lower MTU from their side.

bob_infra: For long-term, we should enable conservative PMTUD fallback (RFC 4821) on internal infra and ensure ICMPv6 rate limits aren't too aggressive on transit. Also consider active probe service for v6 PMTU per AZ.

erin_oncall: Handing off to night oncall @ryan_sre in 40m. Current state: mitigations applied (MTU clamp + LB v6 pref off), error rates down but not fully resolved for high-throughput flows. Next steps for oncall: 1) validate cross-AZ failover plan if errors spike, 2) coordinate with transit partner for PTB forwarding, 3) collect packet captures from customer-facing LBs for deeper trace.

ryan_sre: Taking handoff. I'll keep watch and escalate to netops if we re-escalate. Please drop any queries for me in this thread. :thumbsup:

erin_oncall: Thanks all. Timeline: incident opened 1852009876 (11:36Z). MTU clamp & LB changes at ~11:44Z. Initial recovery signals 11:47Z. Leaving notes in runbook infra/network/runbooks/pmtud-az-mitigation.

netops_sam: Opening ticket with transit peer: TP-4821. They acknowledged and are investigating log drops on their IPv6 control plane.

bob_infra: For postmortem: collect diff of MTU/route config across AZ14 vs AZ15, collect tcpdump captures, rate-limiting stats for ICMPv6, and LB connection-level traces.

katie_prod: Requesting severity classification: I'm proposing Sev3 (partial degradation impacting subset of customers, mitigated by config changes). Agree?

customer_ops: Agrees with Sev3. Customers on paid enterprise plan affected and notified.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: mtu-clamp/az15 -> edge-router-pair (status: success).

ryan_sre: Logging final note before monitoring overnight: keep MTU clamp for 24h, escalate to infra if transit peer doesn't correct PTB forwarding within 6h. If we see >10% error rollback to original and open failover to az16.

erin_oncall: :white_check_mark: Handoff complete. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING. Root cause: PMTUD failures due to selective ICMPv6 PTB suppression across transit paths causing fragmentation/failures for v6 jumbo frames. Mitigation: MTU clamp + v6 preference disabled for affected LBs; next steps: transit partner remediation and PMTUD probes.

ryan_sre: I'll post a short postmortem stub in #postmortems and keep the incident in monitoring until tickets close.

-- end thread --
